samples.summary: XLSX importer's new merge budget enforcement has no test
samples.evidence: `applyMergeRanges` now spends `mergeBudgetOf`/`mergeBudgetAdmits` and silently `continue`s past merges that don't fit, plus maintains a running `budget`. The only merge assertion in packages/sheets/test/import/xlsx-importer.test.ts is line 103 `expect(sheets[0].worksheet.merges?.A1).toEqual({ rs: 1, cs: 2 })` — a single in-budget merge. No fixture exercises an over-budget mergeCell list, so the guard (and the accumulation bug class where `budget` is never incremented) could break with the suite still green.

The new `mergeBudgetAdmits(this.mergeBudget, [span])` check in `canMergeSelection` depends on the `mergeBudget` field that `rebuildMergeCoverMap` now maintains. The only test (packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts:46-51, 'refuses a selection the budget cannot afford') selects MaxMergedCells+1 rows, which is refused by the per-span cap inside `mergeBudgetAdmits` regardless of `this.mergeBudget`. If `this.mergeBudget` were never updated (left at {0,0}), every test still passes — so the field's maintenance and the entry/covered-cell branch have no coverage.
searchedFor: read packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts merge budget describe block

samples.summary: No test for the freeze being released to 0 when the shift-path snap exceeds MaxSnappedFreeze
samples.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges` returns 0 for an axis it cannot settle inside MaxSnappedFreeze, and `shiftWorksheetViewState` / `Sheet.shiftCells` now call it on every insert/delete. The release path is only tested for `setFreezePane` (merge.test.ts 'should release the freeze rather than snap past what the renderer paints'); the added shift tests (worksheet-structure.test.ts and the backend controller spec) only cover small snaps (frozenRows 6, frozenCols 3). An insert/delete silently zeroing a user's freeze is user-visible and untested.

samples.summary: PUT freeze has no test for the case where the snap releases the axis to 0
samples.evidence: `setFreeze` now returns whatever `snapFreezePastMerges` stored, which can be `{rows: 0}` when a merged block is taller than MaxSnappedFreeze. The new spec only covers a snap upward (worksheet.controller.spec.ts: expects `{ rows: 4, cols: 0 }`). An API caller receiving 0 after asking for 2 is a distinct, untested contract.

samples.summary: clearCopyBuffer on sortFilterByColumn is not covered
samples.evidence: The sort path now drops the copy buffer, but packages/sheets/test/sheet/filter.test.ts (lines 203, 226, 260, 325 call sortFilterByColumn) never inspects `getCopyRange()`/`isCutMode()`, and the new copy-buffer lifetime tests in merge.test.ts cover only insert, reorder, undo/redo and remote revalidation. A regression here lets a paste relocate merges from stale coordinates after a sort.

samples.summary: Drag-reorder no longer re-selecting on a refused move is untested
samples.evidence: `movePromise.then((moved) => { if (!moved) return; ... })` changes user-visible selection behavior when a reorder is refused. Sheet-level coverage exists for the boolean (merge.test.ts:1367-1368), but no test exercises the view handler; I found no view-level worksheet drag tests under packages/sheets/test.

samples.summary: Assertion that only restates arithmetic on constants
samples.evidence: `expect(budget.coveredCells + MaxMergedCells).toBeGreaterThan(MaxMergeCoveredCells)` asserts 1e6+1e5 > 1e6 — it exercises no production logic and holds whatever the budget code does. Harmless, but it inflates the apparent coverage of the surrounding 'bounds the map by count, by span, and by their product' test.

samples.summary: Entry-cap test asserts only the return value, not that nothing was written
samples.evidence: 'refuses once the map holds the entry cap' destructures only `store` and asserts `setMerge(...) === false`; unlike the sibling per-span and covered-cell tests it never checks `merges()`, so a refusal that still queued the CRDT write would pass.

samples.summary: snapshotMergesIn's partial-block exclusion filter is untested
samples.evidence: `snapshotMergesIn` filters out blocks the copied range only clips (`isRangeInRange`). All new copy/paste tests select whole blocks (getRangeOrActiveCell expands), so removing the filter would not fail any test. Only reachable programmatically, hence nit.
